title: HeyIris (Iris AI) Pricing in 2026: Per-User Cost, Features, and Reviews
summary: Iris AI (HeyIris) charges per active user with unlimited RFPs, DDQs and proposals. See what a seat includes, who counts as a user, and alternatives.
body_markdown:
Iris AI, sold at heyiris.ai and often called HeyIris, prices per active user. Each paid seat includes unlimited RFPs, proposals, DDQs, and security questionnaires, with no usage caps and no overage fees. Iris explains this model publicly but doesn't list a dollar figure, so you get the number from sales.


Iris is AI RFP software that automates responses to RFPs, RFIs, RFQs, DDQs, security questionnaires, and sales proposals.


The per-user model is simple to grasp, but it is not automatically the cheapest for every team.


This guide breaks down what an Iris seat includes, who counts as a paid user, how per-user cost adds up, and how it compares if you want every contributor in the tool without paying per seat.


## **Key takeaways**


- **Pricing model:** Per active user. One seat covers unlimited RFPs, proposals, DDQs, and security questionnaires, with no usage caps or overages.
- **Who pays:** Anyone who logs in to draft, review, or approve responses counts as an active user. Stakeholders who only view final exports don't need a seat.
- **Price:** Not published. You get a quote from sales, on an annual or multi-year contract, and seats added mid-term are prorated.
- **Reviews:** 4.8/5 on G2. Reviewers praise speed, support, and cited answers, and note that output depends on your documentation and can feel slow on large files.
- **Best fit:** Per-user pricing rewards a small, high-volume team. If many people need to draft or approve, compare it against unlimited-user pricing.


## **How much does Iris AI cost?**


Iris doesn't publish a price, so your seat count decides the bill. It charges for active users, meaning anyone who logs in to draft, review, or approve responses, while people who only view final exports don't need a seat. To size a quote, count everyone who touches a response inside the tool, not just your writers.


On the call, pin down three things: exactly who counts as an active user, whether seats can flex down at renewal, and how seats added mid-term are billed (Iris prorates them for the rest of the billing period). Iris leads with outcomes over price, citing a 60% cut in time per project from one customer and 300+ customers, worth testing against your own numbers.


## **What does one Iris seat include?**


Each paid seat comes with full platform access and unlimited work, so volume never changes the bill. A single seat includes:


- **Unlimited RFx, proposal, DDQ, and security questionnaire work.** RFPs,[RFIs](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/rfi-request-for-information) , RFQs, sales proposals, DDQs, and questionnaires such as CAIQ,[SIG](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/sig-questionnaire-guide) , VSA, and HECVAT, with no per-submission charge.
- **AI qualification and drafting.**[Go/no-go](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/go-no-go-decision-projects) scoring, response generation, and narrative RFP drafting.
- **Compliance checking and**[audit trails](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/inventive-ai-offers-robust-audit-trail-and-version-control-for-your-rfp-responses) **.**
- **Enterprise basics.** SSO, SAML, SCIM, a dedicated customer success manager, implementation support, and MCP access.


The strength of this model is predictability: your cost is set by how many active users you have, not by how many RFPs you run. The variable to watch is headcount, since every person who drafts or approves adds to the price.


## **Per-seat or unlimited users: which pricing model costs your team less?**


This is the real decision behind an Iris quote, and it comes down to the shape of your team. Two models dominate this category, and each rewards a different setup.


- **Per active user (Iris).** You pay for each person who drafts, reviews, or approves, and run unlimited volume. This wins when a small, dedicated team handles a high number of RFPs, because a few seats cover heavy usage.
- **Unlimited users (example:**[Inventive AI](https://www.inventive.ai/inventive-ai-pricing) **).** You pay one published price and give the whole team access. This wins when many people need to be in the tool, because adding an SME or approver never adds a seat.


A quick way to decide: multiply everyone who drafts or approves by a per-seat quote, then compare it to an unlimited-user plan. If your contributor list is long, unlimited users usually lands lower. If two or three power users answer hundreds of documents, per-user can pay off.

## **What features come with every Iris seat?**


HeyIris bundles its full feature set into each paid seat, so there are no add-on modules to buy. Here is what an active user gets.


- **AI qualification (go/no-go).** Scores an incoming RFP against fit before you commit time, so teams can pass on low-odds bids early. **‍**
- **AI response generation and narrative drafting.** Drafts question-and-answer responses, longer narrative RFP sections, and sales proposals from your content. **‍**
- **Source citations and confidence scores.** Each answer links back to the source passage it draws from, and confidence scores flag responses that need a closer look. **‍**
- **Automated**[compliance checking](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/proposal-compliance-matrix-guide) **.** Checks a response for coverage against the requirements before it goes out, which matters most on security questionnaires and regulated bids.
- **Knowledge sources and content freshness.** The Knowledge Map connects Salesforce, HubSpot, SharePoint, Google Drive, Confluence, Notion, Gong, Vanta, and Drata, and flags aging or expiring content for review.
- **Unlimited RFx, DDQ, and security questionnaires.** One seat covers RFPs, RFIs,[RFQs](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/rfq-management-software-a-complete-guide) ,[DDQs](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/ddq-meaning) , and security frameworks like CAIQ, SIG, VSA, and HECVAT, with no per-submission fee. **‍**
- **MCP access.** Connects Iris to ChatGPT, Claude, and other tools through the Model Context Protocol. **‍**
- **Collaboration and audit trails.** Shared drafting, review steps, and a record of who changed what, useful for regulated or audited responses. **‍**
- **Exports.** Push finished responses back into the original format for submission. **‍**
- **Enterprise access and support.** SSO, SAML, and SCIM for provisioning, plus a dedicated customer success manager and implementation support. **‍**
- **MCP access.** Connects HeyIris to other tools through the Model Context Protocol for teams that want to extend it.


## **HeyIris review, ratings, strengths and weaknesses**


HeyIris holds a 4.8/5 rating on[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/heyiris-ai-iris/reviews) , so most teams that use it are happy. Here's what reviewers consistently praise, and where they hit friction.


### **What reviewers like about Iris**


- Fast first drafts. Iris pulls from your past content and fills a questionnaire in minutes, which is the main reason teams buy it.
- Simple to learn. Reviewers call the interface clean and say onboarding is quick, so new team members contribute without much ramp-up.
- Responsive support. Users mention the team ships fixes and takes feedback seriously.


### **Where teams find limitations in Iris**


- Responses can read robotic. Reviewers note the output often needs a human pass to sound like your company and match the buyer's tone.
- Quality depends on your library. If your source content is thin or outdated, the drafts reflect that. Iris speeds up retrieval, it does not fix the content underneath.
- Struggles with nuance. Complex, technical, or visual questions still need an expert, and reviewers flag occasional slowness and bugs.
- No mobile app. Everything happens on desktop, which some reviewers wanted.
- Can feel slow. Reviewers note processing lag on large or complex documents, which hurts under tight deadlines.


### **Questions worth confirming on a demo**


Ask the questions that decide your real cost and review load: exactly who counts as an active user, whether approvers need a paid seat, how seats added mid-term are billed, and whether Iris flags when two sources contradict each other rather than only when content ages. Run one of your own RFPs through the proof of concept to check tone and turnaround.


### **Who is Iris best for?**


Iris fits a small, dedicated RFP or security team that runs high volume and wants predictable per-seat cost with unlimited usage. It is a weaker fit for organizations where many people need to draft or approve inside the tool, that want cost to stay flat as headcount grows, or that have thin or scattered documentation for the AI to draw on.

## Frequently Asked Questions


### Is HeyIris the same as Iris AI?


Yes. Iris is the product, sold at heyiris.ai by Iris AI Technologies, and many buyers still search for it as HeyIris. The pricing, features, and reviews on this page apply to both names.


### Who counts as an active user in Iris?


Anyone who logs in to draft, review, or approve responses counts as an active user and needs a paid seat. Stakeholders who only view final exports don't count, but confirm the definition in writing, since it sets your seat total.


### Are Iris seats added mid-contract prorated?


Yes. Seats you add during the contract are prorated for the rest of the billing period, so you pay only for the time left rather than a full year.


### Does Iris offer multi-year contracts?


Yes. Iris sells annual and multi-year agreements, and longer terms can lower the price, though it doesn't publish the discount. Ask for the per-seat rate under each term length before you commit.


### Does Iris offer a free trial?


Not a self-serve one. Iris offers a guided evaluation and proof of concept, and its free RFP analyzer lets you test go/no-go scoring on a past RFP before you talk to sales.


### Does Iris charge extra for proposals or portal work?


Iris's pricing page lists full platform access on each active seat, including unlimited proposals alongside RFPs, DDQs, and security questionnaires. Confirm in your quote that portal workflows and MCP access carry no separate fee.
